findings.title: Added contacts do not persist after page reload
steps: 1. Open http://localhost:9906 — 3 seed contacts shown (Alice, Bob, Carol)
2. Click 'Add Contact', fill Name='Dana Test', Email='dana@example.com', Phone='+1 555-0199', click Save
3. 'Dana Test' appears as the 4th contact; count shows '4 contacts'
4. Reload the page (navigate to http://localhost:9906 again)
5. List reverts to 3 seed contacts; 'Dana Test' is gone; count shows '3 contacts'
findings.expected: The newly added contact should persist across a page reload, since the app's stated requirement is 'Add a contact, save it, reload the page, and verify the contact persists.' The contact list and count should remain '4 contacts' including 'Dana Test'.
findings.actual: After reload, the contact list reverts to the original 3 seed contacts and 'Dana Test' is lost. The count drops from 4 back to 3. The app stores data only in memory and re-seeds on every load, so no user-created contacts survive a reload.
findings.observed: Post-reload body text reads '3 contacts' with only Alice Johnson, Bob Smith, and Carol White. The Dana Test contact added moments before is no longer present.
findings.impact: The core function of a contact management app is to store contacts permanently. Because nothing persists, every contact a user adds is silently destroyed on refresh, making the app unusable for its intended purpose.
findings.recommendation: Persist contacts to durable storage (localStorage, IndexedDB, or a backend database) and load from that store on init instead of re-seeding the default list on every page load. Only seed defaults when the store is empty/uninitialized.

findings.title: Phone number entered in the Add Contact form is never displayed or stored
steps: 4. Inspect the newly created contact card in the list
findings.expected: The contact card should display the phone number that was entered in the Phone field, and the phone value should be stored as part of the contact record.
findings.actual: After saving, the contact card renders only two spans — Name and Email. The phone number is never displayed anywhere in the UI. The card structure (div > div > span[1]=name, span[2]=email) contains no element for phone, so the value entered into the Phone field is silently discarded on save.
findings.observed: New 'Phone Check' contact card shows only 'Phone Check' and 'phone@example.com'. The phone value '+1 555-9999' is absent from the entire page.
findings.impact: Users who rely on phone numbers lose that data silently — they type it, it appears to save, but the number is never stored or shown. For a contact manager, phone numbers are a primary field, so this is significant data loss.
findings.recommendation: Store the phone value in the contact object in the save handler and render a third span/element in the contact card template to display it.
